hypothesis: Empirical cross-subject and cross-muscle validation of local bioenergetics model can be achieved without verified raw human time-series.

hypothesis: Hug et al. 2021 reported Gastrocnemius Medialis discharge rates of 9.8, 12.6, 15.4, and 19.8 Hz across 8 independent human participants.
result: Refuted: Table 2 of Hug et al. 2021 preprint and journal publication reports GM mean discharge rates of 8.1, 8.1, 7.6, and 12.2 pps after manual editing. The eight operators were rater co-authors evaluating shared recordings from an unknown number of male participants across two reused experiments. N=8 raters != 8 subjects.
impact: Retracted unconfirmed discharge rates; replaced with published Table 2 numbers; classified biological sample size as UNKNOWN; barred equating operators with independent biological subjects.

hypothesis: More than 99% of energy in a 45-minute 250 W whole-body test is supplied oxidatively based on the ratio of single-muscle static PCr buffer to external mechanical work.
result: Refuted: Dividing single-muscle local PCr buffer capacity (0.62 kJ) by whole-body external mechanical work (675 kJ) commits a category error between static local capacity and dynamic whole-body flux, confounds mechanical work with gross metabolic expenditure (~3375 kJ), and ignores systemic anaerobic glycolysis (~75 kJ) and multi-muscle recruitment.
impact: Enforces multi-dimensional energetic accounting separating mechanical work, metabolic cost, ATP turnover, oxidative resynthesis, and glycolysis; bars invalid >99% oxidative claims for TARGET-CPE45.

hypothesis: Nominal exercise protocol timing (fitting from 90s nominal stop) reproduces true recovery kinetics, prospective prediction from t=90s is achievable without workload/perfusion data, model M2 validates multi-scale physiological balance, intracellular pH universally satisfies pH >= 6.86, and arbitrary MR signal amplitudes can identify absolute resting PCr concentration and active muscle volume.
result: Refuted across multiple dimensions: (1) Fitting from nominal 90s stop instead of actual biochemical nadir contaminates recovery with ongoing exercise depletion, underestimating k by 20-33% and degrading fit quality; (2) Prospective prediction (Scenario B) from t=90s prior to observing future nadir and post-exercise lag is blocked (PROSPECTIVE_PREDICTION_BLOCKED_UNOBSERVED_DEPLETION_DYNAMICS) because depletion depth and duration cannot be inferred without work rate or perfusion data; (3) Model M2 is mathematically a constrained monoexponential baseline model, not a validated multi-scale physiological ODE; full model M3 cannot be executed on relative MRS alone (M3_NOT_EXECUTABLE_ON_AVAILABLE_OBSERVATIONS); (4) Universal non-acidosis claim pH >= 6.86 is refuted by calculated minimum pH of 6.7932 in Trial 1 (range 6.7932-7.0228); (5) Arbitrary MR signal amplitudes are intrinsically scale-confounded with receiver coil sensitivity and cannot identify absolute mM concentration; (6) Single-coil MRS creates an exact unidentifiable scaling symmetry between active muscle volume and localized metabolic depletion; (7) Cross-subject LOSO validation is mathematically impossible on an N=1 cohort.
impact: Mandates empirical nadir detection for phase alignment; blocks prospective forward simulation without work rate/perfusion inputs; reclassifies M2 as constrained monoexponential; marks M3 as unexecutable on available data; retracts pH >= 6.86; maintains absolute PCr concentration and active volume as strictly unidentifiable; prohibits cross-subject generalization from single-participant MRS.

hypothesis: Successful multi-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out validation of macroscopic aerobic bioenergetic coupling (P_mech -> VO2) on cycle ergometry constitutes empirical validation of the full multi-scale physiological ODE (M3), identifies localized intracellular high-energy phosphate dynamics ([PCr], [Pi], [ATP], cytosolic pH), validates motor unit recruitment order, and validates extreme 45-minute survival (TARGET-CPE45).
result: Refuted: Whole-body pulmonary oxygen consumption and crank mechanical power represent volume-integrated macroscopic observables. By the many-to-one mapping (entanglement fallacy), an infinite manifold of localized muscle recruitment patterns, regional perfusion states, and intracellular phosphate depletion curves yield the identical systemic VO2 curve. Therefore, ACTES CPET data strictly cannot identify localized [PCr], [Pi], or pH dynamics (which remain bounded by Rehman 2024 N=1), cannot observe motor unit discharge rates (which remain bounded by Hug 2021), and cannot validate TARGET-CPE45, which requires a dedicated continuous 45-minute endurance test rather than a 15-minute incremental graded ramp to exhaustion.
impact: Prevents false claims of full physiological model validation. Strictly confines ACTES validation to macroscopic aerobic efficiency (eta_gross) and Phase II response kinetics (tau). Establishes REMAINING_BARRIERS_MATRIX and maintains TARGET-CPE45 as NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions as NO_GO.

hypothesis: Single-variable linear body mass scaling (P/M) universally improves prediction across all individual human subjects, and macroscopic cycling efficiency parameters (delta efficiency eta_delta, regression slope beta1) directly transfer to running locomotion without modality-specific calibration via an ad-hoc linear velocity-to-power multiplier.
result: Refuted on two empirical grounds: (1) In the ACTES cycling cohort (EXP-0043), while linear mass normalization improves macro-average R2 across the full cohort, it worsens prediction RMSE in 7 of the 18 participants (Subjects 3, 4, 6, 15, 16, 17, 18), demonstrating that simple linear mass scaling introduces individual bias for light endurance and heavy muscular athletes; (2) In the Malaga treadmill cohort (EXP-0044, N=981 valid tests across N=846 independent participants), applying the naive formula pred_vo2 = 560 + (7.657 * 25.0) * speed incurs a severe error penalty (GroupKFold RMSE = 584.9 mL/min, R2 = 0.2465, RMSE penalty = +180.8 mL/min vs M4). This failure is classified as AD_HOC_CROSS_MODAL_MAPPING_FAILURE because the 25 W/(km/h) factor is an arbitrary construct rather than measured running mechanical power. True physical cross-modal transfer is classified as PHYSICAL_CROSS_MODAL_TRANSFER_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE due to lack of mechanical power, ground reaction forces, and tendon elastic recoil data.
impact: Prohibits universal application of uncalibrated linear body mass scaling without individual body composition accounting; bars arbitrary linear conversion of running speed to cycling mechanical power; reclassifies cross-modal transfer failure into AD_HOC_CROSS_MODAL_MAPPING_FAILURE and sets PHYSICAL_CROSS_MODAL_TRANSFER_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE; mandates modality-specific biomechanical locomotion models.

hypothesis: Single-muscle vastus lateralis knee extension torque, sEMG amplitude, and ultrasound fascicle length directly predict whole-body maximum strength and athletic capacity, and successful validation of 20-minute intermittent fatigue compensation models provides empirical validation for continuous 45-minute extreme metabolic endurance (TARGET-CPE45).
result: Refuted on three physiological and biomechanical grounds: (1) Decoupling in Dynamic Motion: Active joint torque cannot be inferred from static sEMG (R2 = 0.118 on active points, pub 0.13) or static fascicle strain (R2 = 0.016 on active points, pub 0.01), refuting static muscle proxy models. (2) Indeterminacy of Net Joint Moment: Knee dynamometer torque (N*m) conflates four distinct quadriceps heads, antagonist hamstring co-contraction, and variable patellar tendon moment arm (3.5 to 4.8 cm); converting joint torque to single-muscle force requires unobserved load-sharing assumptions. (3) Protocol and Epistemic Incommensurability: Neuromuscular compensation (+26% activation increase at 45% MVC) over 20 minutes of intermittent contractions does not measure intracellular high-energy phosphate depletion ([PCr], [ATP], [Pi]), cytosolic acidosis (pH), or whole-body metabolic heat flux, and strictly cannot validate continuous 45-minute steady-state extreme endurance (TARGET-CPE45, 2700 s at 250 W). TARGET-CPE45 remains NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions strictly NO_GO.
impact: Prohibits using isolated single-muscle dynamometry or static proxies to extrapolate whole-body performance; prohibits claiming that 20-minute submaximal fatigue validates continuous 45-minute extreme endurance TARGET-CPE45; preserves strict epistemic boundaries on tissue-level vs whole-body observables.

hypothesis: Raw UWB radar frequency reflection features directly generalize across unseen human subjects to predict knee extension torque (%MVC) without subject-specific calibration, and single engineered composite feature M4 provides a superior cross-subject predictive model over simple linear sEMG baseline M1.
result: Refuted across two rigorous empirical evaluations on Bird et al. (2026) raw dynamic arrays (DATA_Dynamic_Knee.mat, 3,226 observations, N=6; torque in fraction of MVC [0.0, 1.0], partitioned into 1,382 passive protocol and 1,844 active protocol observations): (1) Radar Generalization Collapse: The specific uncalibrated UWB Ridge regression model (204 frequency channels) collapses from intra-participant 5-fold CV R2 = 0.9763 +/- 0.0097 to cross-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) R2 = -2.4457 +/- 2.2077 (NRMSE = 47.25%), failing on 5 of 6 held-out human participants. Comprehensive sensitivity analysis confirms that this collapse persists across all Ridge regularizations (alpha from 0.001 to 1000), inner-fold standard/robust scalers, frequency subsets (S11 R2 = -0.8431, S21 R2 = -9.5060, Mag R2 = -0.7495, Phase R2 = -2.5501), and active protocol runs (R2 = -6.0154). This collapse is confined to this linear Ridge implementation and must not be extrapolated to declare all UWB technologies unusable, nor to non-linear architectures (LME, LSTM, RF) without explicit LOSO validation. (2) Engineered Feature M4 Evaluation: Cross-subject LOSO evaluation of the single engineered feature model M4 (R2 = 0.3251 +/- 0.0946, NRMSE = 21.93%) yields only a statistically insignificant +0.0148 delta R2 over standard Hill model M3 (R2 = 0.3103 +/- 0.0819; paired t = 1.080, p = 0.3294, 95% CI [-0.0204, +0.0501]), which does NOT prove equivalence. Relative to M1 sEMG baseline (R2 = 0.4628 +/- 0.0651), the observed sample point-estimate favors M1 by +0.1377 (Delta R2 = -0.1377), but this difference is NOT statistically significant at two-sided alpha=0.05 (paired t = -2.462, p = 0.0571; Wilcoxon p = 0.0625; 95% CI [-0.2814, +0.0061] spans zero) due to limited power (N=6). The negative result is formally designated ENGINEERED_FEATURE_M4_NO_VERIFIED_ADVANTAGE. The full multi-scale physiological ODE architecture of SUBJECT-01 is NOT evaluated in this linear feature test and remains unfalsified (FULL_SUBJECT01_MULTISCALE_ARCHITECTURE_NOT_FALSIFIED_BY_THIS_TEST).
impact: Bars claiming cross-subject generalizability for raw uncalibrated UWB radar; bars declaring engineered feature M4 superior to baseline sEMG M1 on raw human dynamometry (ENGINEERED_FEATURE_M4_NO_VERIFIED_ADVANTAGE); preserves FULL_SUBJECT01_MULTISCALE_ARCHITECTURE_NOT_FALSIFIED_BY_THIS_TEST; mandates subject-specific calibration for RF-based biomechanical models; preserves negative result in repository registry.

hypothesis: An isolated +20% increase in contractile muscle fiber force directly yields a +20% increase in net functional joint torque without neural co-activation tuning or pennation angle losses.
result: MODEL_ONLY. With fixed gamma and all other scenario assumptions, a +2.8 degree pennation change lowers cos(alpha) by 1.38% relative to nominal. Simulated +20% fiber force yields +18.34% net knee torque. The 8.3% is the share of the planned torque gain lost under this scenario.
impact: Treat geometry and antagonist moment separately. Their empirical dose-response and necessity for meeting the target remain unverified.

result: Comprehensive global audit across Zenodo, Dryad, Figshare, PhysioNet, SimTK, AddBiomechanics, and UCI identified 0 qualified datasets. Bird 2026 lacked antagonists; Wang 2022 used locomotion with inverse-dynamics moments; UCI 278 lacked torque transducers. Experiment E1 is DATA_BLOCKED.

result: Comprehensive audit identified 0 qualified datasets. Kongsgaard et al. (2007) deposited only aggregate cohort means (104, 118, 127 mm2); raw individual data was never deposited. Substituting literature means as individual data is prohibited as unscientific. Experiment E2 is DATA_BLOCKED.
impact: HYP-0010 remains unverified. Tendon stress concentration at the proximal insertion (38.46 MPa baseline, 46.15 MPa at +20% force) confirmed theoretically, causing an estimated 60-75% reduction in cyclic fatigue life.

hypothesis: An independent third public human adult MTJ transcriptomic dataset exists to replicate the frozen MTJCore myonuclear program.
result: Systematic audit across GEO, ArrayExpress, CELLxGENE, and GSA-Human identified 0 open independent cohorts outside Copenhagen. E-MTAB-12529 is discovery; E-MTAB-15400 already failed in Stage 6 (0.5818 < 0.60); E-MTAB-12530 has identical donors; HRA002803 is controlled-access. Experiment E5 is DATA_BLOCKED.
impact: MTJCore cannot be claimed as a replicated universal marker of tissue strength. Directional RNA concordance does not equal protein translation or mechanical tensile strength.

title: Failure of Uncalibrated Surface Antagonist EMG to Improve Cross-Subject Isometric Torque Estimation
statement: Adding uncalibrated antagonist hamstrings surface EMG (M2) to an agonist-only OLS model (M1) failed to achieve statistically significant improvement in Leave-One-Subject-Out prediction error across 20 adults (Delta RMSE = -3.94 Nm, paired t-test p = 0.1426, Wilcoxon p = 0.2863).
reason: Antagonist co-activation magnitude is low (~8-11% of agonist amplitude) and subject to inter-individual skin impedance variance, causing unregularized cross-subject models to fit individual noise.

title: Impossibility of Mechanical Stress Determination in Bogaerts Cohort Due to Absent Layer CSA
statement: Full mechanical validation of HYP-0010 (regional stress distribution) was blocked in Bogaerts et al. (2017) because individual sub-tendon cross-sectional areas were not measured, preventing conversion of force into engineering stress.
reason: Ultrasound imaging was restricted to sagittal 2D displacement tracking without transverse axial sub-tendon morphometry.

title: Inability to Replicate Myonuclear MTJCore Program on Oxford Achilles Single-Cell Atlas
statement: Attempted replication of Karlsen's myonuclear MTJCore signature on Cohen et al. (2026) was blocked due to cell-type boundary: Cohen et al. dissociated and isolated tendon fibroblasts/tenocytes only, with zero myonuclei present in the dataset.
reason: Surgical dissection protocols removed skeletal muscle myofibers to enrich for tendon fibroblasts, precluding myonuclear evaluation.

title: Falsification of Surface EMG Predictive Value in Cross-Subject Population Models
statement: Adding surface EMG features to anthropometric and kinematic variables increased cross-subject prediction error across all tested algorithms (OLS and Ridge), with antagonist EMG significantly degrading RMSE (p = 0.0089).
reason: Subcutaneous adipose filtering and skin impedance differences create inter-individual noise that overwhelms the small co-activation torque signal.

title: Falsification of Layer-Specific Active Tendon Strain Heterogeneity at Subject Level
statement: Subject-level aggregation (N=10) of Bogaerts ultrasound speckle tracking during isometric plantarflexion refuted the hypothesis of layer-dependent strain differences (Friedman chi2 = 0.80, p = 0.6703).
reason: Prior claims of strain heterogeneity in Cycle 16 were an artifact of 4-fold pseudoreplication treating repeated trials as independent subjects.

title: Inability to Replicate MTJCore on Oxford Single-Cell Atlas Due to Missing Donor Pseudobulk Tables
statement: Independent replication of the frozen Karlsen MTJCore signature on Cohen et al. (2026) was blocked because public DEG tables isolate fibroblast subtypes and lack donor-level myonuclear pseudobulk counts.
reason: Primary study prioritized stromal fibroblast specialization and did not provide donor-level non-junctional control contrast matrices.

title: Oxford Achilles Atlas Ineligible for Third Independent Replication of MTJCore
statement: Independent biological replication of MTJCore on the Oxford Achilles Atlas is invalid due to dataset identity with the discovery training cohort (100% data leakage). In the global public domain, no third independent snRNA-seq cohort with donor-level adult human MTJ contrasts exists. MTJCore replication attempts on Cohen et al. are closed with decision STOP_NO_ADDED_SCIENTIFIC_VALUE.
reason: Data provenance audit proved that Cohen et al. (2026) was the original discovery cohort of MTJCore.

title: Stromal COL22A1 Upregulation Fails Preregistered Donor Consistency Threshold
statement: In the Achilles MTJ-vs-midbody fibroblast contrast, COL22A1 upregulation achieved a donor direction consistency of only 0.60 (elevated in 3 of 5 donors), failing the preregistered threshold of >= 0.75 and resulting in rejection from the frozen fibroblast signature. Hypothesis HYP-0013 lacks novelty as cellular distributions were already published in Cohen et al. (2026).
reason: Inter-donor inconsistency in stromal COL22A1 expression and lack of originality relative to published literature.

title: Isomass Pennation Scaling Trade-Off: Force Gain Sacrifices Shortening Velocity and Range of Motion
statement: In human skeletal muscle under fixed total mass/volume (isomass constraint), increasing pennation angle theta from 14 deg to 18 deg increases PCSA and isometric force by +25.2% (from 6059 N to 7586 N), but causes an unavoidable geometric reduction of -21.7% in maximum shortening velocity (v_max drops from 8.84 to 6.92 l_0/s) and joint active range of motion due to reduced fiber length l_f. Pure pennation remodeling cannot achieve +20% force without dynamic performance penalties.
reason: Constant-volume geometric constraint: V = PCSA * l_f = const. Increasing PCSA proportionally shortens fascicle length l_f, reducing the number of sarcomeres in series and maximum shortening speed.

title: Tendon Elastic Modulus Remodeling Without Hypertrophy Yields Zero Fatigue Life Gain
statement: Under a +20% augmented muscle force, increasing tendon elastic modulus E by +15% without cross-sectional area hypertrophy (Delta CSA = 0) produces exactly 0% improvement in cyclic fatigue life (N_cycles remains 0.133x baseline, -86.7% loss). While tendon stiffness increases, peak engineering tensile stress sigma = F / CSA remains unattenuated at 48.74 MPa, proving that material stiffening without geometric hypertrophy is ineffective for tendon fatigue protection.
reason: Wöhler S-N fatigue life is governed by cyclic peak tensile stress sigma relative to ultimate tensile strength UTS. Altering elastic modulus affects strain at load but leaves stress identical if CSA is unchanged.

title: Falsification of Isolated In Vivo Specific Tension Identifiability from Joint Dynamometry Without Subject-Specific Volumetry
statement: Global uncertainty quantification (Monte Carlo N=10,000) across anthropometric, kinematic, and allometric parameters revealed that in vivo specific tension calculated from joint dynamometry alone has a 95% credibility interval of [17.58, 44.98] N/cm2 (uncertainty span 27.41 N/cm2). Specific tension cannot be claimed as an independently measured scalar for individual subjects without co-acquired 3D-MRI muscle volumetry, B-mode ultrasound fascicle tracking, and interpolated twitch activation measurements.
reason: Dynamometer net joint torque reflects an indeterminate product of moment arm, muscle volume, fascicle length, pennation, antagonist co-contraction, and central voluntary drive.

title: Falsification of Fine-Scale Biological Equivalence Between Sexes in Muscle Specific Tension at 10% Margin
statement: Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) on N=20 adults (10 males, 10 females, DPValid) failed to establish statistical equivalence of quadriceps specific tension at a +/- 10% equivalence margin (p_TOST = 0.1449 > 0.05). While Welch's t-test yielded p = 0.8981 (failing to reject equality of means: male 26.27 vs female 26.55 N/cm2), concluding biological equivalence requires an expanded statistical power. Equivalence is statistically supported only at a broader +/- 20% margin (p_TOST = 0.0169).
reason: Failure to reject a null hypothesis of difference in a Student's t-test does not constitute proof of equivalence.

title: External Bilateral Leg Press Cohort Absence (DATA_BLOCKED), Naive Pseudoinverse Incompatibility, and Inconclusive Single-Joint DPValid Precision
statement: Open search and gate audit across 6 candidate repositories (OpenCap, Zoger 2025, Zushi 2024, Zenodo 6503956, Figshare 33936784/PLOS 0357488, Zenodo 23979972/Frontiers 1948872) yielded 0 admitted cohorts for external validation of bilateral isometric leg press (Outcome 4: DATA_BLOCKED). Naive 3-DOF closed-chain assignment (a=0.95) is physically incompatible (point-contact overdetermination residual 253.68 Nm at 100 deg; flat-foot COP = +0.1706 m > +0.16 m boundary). On single-joint DPValid (N=20), all pairwise paired cluster bootstrap 95% CIs relative to proposed Delta_min = 0.08 cross the threshold (M2 vs F0 [+0.0259, +0.1428], M2 vs M1 [-0.0903, +0.1173], Outcome 3: INCONCLUSIVE).
reason: Zoger 2025 raw data are available upon request only; allometric volume regression is nearly collinear with age/mass/height/sex on N=20 participants.

title: Heterochrony Damage Spike Under TARGET-ADAPT25 and Ballistic 100% MVC Enthesis Margin Breach Under Rapid dF/dt
statement: Accelerating muscular adaptation speed (+25%, tau_m = 12 d) ahead of slow tendon collagen remodeling (tau_t = 90 d) induces a transient 2.94x peak daily fatigue damage spike around week 3.0 (48 days > 2.0x baseline hazard). At maximal 100% MVC ballistic tension (7661 N, dF/dt = 20,000 N/s), localized deep-layer enthesis von Mises stress reaches 92.20 MPa (> 85 MPa collagen threshold, SF_local = 1.03) unadapted, and remains at 79.91 MPa (SF_local = 1.31 < 1.50 safety gate) even after Case 2C (+15% CSA, +10% UTS).
reason: Tendon collagen turnover half-life limits safe adaptation velocity (BLOCKER-03), and deep-layer shear concentration + viscoelastic rate stiffening erode nominal uniaxial safety margins (BLOCKER-02).

title: Continuous +20% Work Thermal Breach Across Climates and AEGIS-01 Evaporative Barrier Penalty
statement: Continuous unpaced output at 360 W (1436.3 W total heat) breaches the 39.5 C core safety limit across all tested climates >= 20 C within 1240 to 2365 s (reaching 39.81 C at 20 C and 42.77 C at 35 C), while 300 W breaches 39.5 C in all warm/hot climates >= 28 C (1625 to 2335 s). Imposing the AEGIS-01 keratinized barrier (-35% skin evaporative/convective conductance, +2 kg) cuts safe temperate duty cycle capacity D_max by -14.0% at 300 W (1.00 -> 0.86) and -25.0% at 360 W (0.92 -> 0.69), confirming PR #9 CONDITIONAL HOLD.
reason: Human evaporative cooling capacity (~580-750 W effective ceiling with sweat drip) cannot sustain continuous 1200-1450 W metabolic heat loads.

title: Equal-work control removes the large thermal contrast
statement: At identical external work, the modeled intermittent minus constant peak core difference is -0.058 to +0.001 C across reported conditions and time steps; the sign changes in the temperate scenario. Equal-work pairs all pass the archived model gate. No model-independent or functional benefit is established.
reason: Original full-power comparator changes scheduled work, while results at equal work are small and partly sensitive to model or time step.

title: Frozen Pennes model loses to persistence on held-out light cycling
statement: 35 sessions from 6 participants. Participant-average MAE is 0.429 C for the unchanged model vs 0.251 C for persistence, paired base-minus-model bootstrap 95% CI [-0.286, -0.080] C. Limited transfer gate fails at all tested humidity assumptions.
reason: Scope is the locked initial state and parameterization on a protocol-shift dataset; starting tissue temperatures, actual mechanical traces and humidity were unavailable. No inference about 2700-s performance.

title: Cross-protocol first-two-sprint model fails against persistence
statement: Training the late-sprint ratio model on Chmura and applying to 21 previously viewed Jutlah participants gives participant-weighted MAE 138.98 W against 95.36 W for first-sprint persistence. Paired MAE difference persistence minus linear [-80.41,-10.07] W. Within-cohort LOSO intervals cross zero.
reason: Different rest intervals, populations and task context are confounded; no unique causal mechanism inferred.
